assumptions: The ported alternation core lives in ts/src/util/alternation.ts rather than ts/src/history/detector.ts as the spec's 'Where it lives' says. Two reasons: core/ci-ready.ts must read the same computation (spec D9) and core -> history is a layer violation harness check-deps rejects, which is the same reason Phase 1 put flake-window.ts in util/; and ts/src/history's top-level module-size budget had no room for it.

The per-test 8-observation minimum (D5/H2) is rendered as a three-valued alternating field: true / false / null, where null is UNKNOWN. The spec named the minimum but not its representation; null reuses Phase 1's UNKNOWN-is-not-zero doctrine rather than inventing a second vocabulary.

The observation minimum gates the CLEAN verdict only. A test already observed changing and changing back is reported whatever its sample size, since withholding an observed finding would be its own false green.
A row is included when it crosses the threshold on EITHER axis. The spec requires SC6's alternator to be listed while its flake rate is 0, which cannot happen under a flake-rate-only filter.
queryFlaky now sorts records by timestamp before windowing, per the spec's 'Ordering by timestamp' accepted risk. Runs with no timestamp keep their append order (the sort is stable).
The Supabase flip disclosure is keyed off the same optional-readAll capability split Phase 1 used for runs_read, so flips_measured is false exactly where runs_read is null.

The TS-Python parity goldens are left as captured; the new Flip % / Flips/Observed columns are stripped from the flaky section before comparison and pinned in their own assertion, which is the precedent Phase 1 set for its window preamble.
